key_grammar.point: 배수 원급비교 twice as much as
key_grammar.source_sentence: In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to donate money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they'd made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to recall previous bad deeds.

explanation.text: 'twice as much as ~'는 '~보다 두 배 많은/많이'라는 뜻으로, 배수사 twice를 원급 비교 as ~ as 바로 앞에 붙인 형태다.
배수사(twice·three times…) + as + 원급(much·many·big) + as + 비교 대상.
셀 수 없는 양(돈·수입)은 much, 셀 수 있는 것(책·사람)은 many를 쓴다: twice as much money / twice as many books.
half·twice 같은 배수사는 비교급(more·-er) 앞에는 쓰지 못하고 반드시 원급 as ~ as와 함께 쓴다.

key_grammar.example: She earns twice as much money as I do.
key_grammar.example_analysis: gave ... almost twice as much as those ~ : 배수사 twice가 원급 비교 as much as 앞에 붙어 '거의 두 배'를 나타낸다.

drills.question: 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?
drills.sentence: In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects [[1|who]] wrote down a list of past good deeds and [[2|were then asked]] [[3|to donate]] money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they'd made from the study — almost [[4|twice as many as]] those who [[5|had been instructed]] to recall previous bad deeds.
drills.fix: money/earnings는 셀 수 없는 양이므로 many → much로 고쳐 twice as much as로 써야 한다.

drills.question: 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 것을 고르시오.
drills.sentence: Simply [[perceiving/perceive]] ourselves as people [[who/whom]] do good deeds and behaving accordingly [[motivates/motivate]] us to do greater good in the future.
drills.fix: 문장의 주어가 동명사(perceiving)여야 하고, 주격 관계대명사 who, 동명사 주어는 단수 취급이므로 motivates이다.

drills.question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
drills.answer: ③ According to the study, the motivation to do good deeds were more evident in those who recalled their past virtues and those who focused purely on their good deeds than those who recalled their previous bad deeds and those who seemed highly conscious of the appearances of their deeds.
drills.fix: 주어 the motivation이 단수이므로 were → was로 고쳐야 한다.
options: ① Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior.
② Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future.

③ According to the study, the motivation to do good deeds were more evident in those who recalled their past virtues and those who focused purely on their good deeds than those who recalled their previous bad deeds and those who seemed highly conscious of the appearances of their deeds.

④ In addition, subjects who'd taken pains to describe not only how they'd been nice to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves.

⑤ In other words, people who seemed concerned about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less generous than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.

drills.question: 그는 그의 형보다 두 배 많은 책을 읽었다. (배수 원급비교 사용)
drills.answer: He read twice as many books as his brother.

drills.question: 우리의 성인 뇌는 선하고 공정한 행동을 지속하려는 선호를 유지한다.
drills.answer: Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior.
